text:
alex: Heads up — after the batch-scheduler v2 deploy we saw a 25% tail-latency regression for qwen2.5 on mixed-language workloads.
maya: saw that alert too. repro is easy: alternate short CJK prompt then long english paragraph.
rachel: interesting, did the kernel chooser flip?
perf-bot: profiler snapshot 2475006801: kernel_selector=autokernel, latency_p50=72ms, latency_p95=220ms, kv_cache_hits=0.58
alex: here's a quick log snippet from the runtime when the switch happens:
```
[2026-08-12T14:13:21Z] request=abcd kernel=fast_attn kv_tag=shardA tokenizer=byte-level
[2026-08-12T14:13:21Z] request=abcd kernel_selector->autokernel reason=ropescale_mismatch score=-3.2
[2026-08-12T14:13:22Z] kv_cache: invalidated shards=[shardA] reason=tokenizer-switch
[2026-08-12T14:13:22Z] kernel_change: new=autokernel path=~/kernels/autokernel_x64.so latency_est=1.8x
```
maya: kv_cache invalidation on tokenizer switch — that's a red flag. our kv-tagging relies on vocab-id continuity. switching from CJK tokens to long Latin sequence flips subtokenization and we drop tags.
rachel: could be the heuristic introduced to favor autokernel when rope_scale_delta > 0.12 — for multilingual bursts it flips too eagerly.
alex: repro script attached in thread: run 100 alternating requests, measure kernel usages. I get kernel_flip_count ~ 47/100 and p95 jump ~180ms.
maya: quick mitigation: bump rope_scale_delta threshold to 0.2 in canary and add a sticky-window of 2 requests to avoid churn.
rachel: agree. alternative is to make KV shards tolerant: keep shard mapping for N tokens across tokenizer boundary if embedding dim unchanged.
perf-bot: perf diff (canary run): baseline batch-scheduler v1 p95=130ms, v2 candidate p95=210ms, sticky-window=2 p95=145ms.
deploy-bot: deploy request: rollback candidate -> batch-scheduler v1? (runbook says canary -> global).
alex: propose small hotfix: revert the aggressive rope-scale heuristic and enable sticky-window. I'll open a PR with tests.
maya: also add a unit test that simulates CJK->Latin token boundary and asserts kv_tag continuity.
rachel: for long term, we should tune kernel_selector scoring to penalize kernel flips when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.5.
alex: noted. next steps: alex will open PR, maya will create canary with sticky-window flag, rachel will run 1h perf run on mixed-lang corpora.
maya: timeline?
alex: PR by EOD, canary tonight, perf run tomorrow morning. ping me if regressions persist. :thumbsup:
rachel: thanks — good catch by the alerting threshold.
perf-bot: recorded incident id perf-20260812-17 for followup.
deploy-bot: rollback scheduled at 2475006880: batch-scheduler v1 restored.
